articles.title: Germany settlement permit: What it is, benefits and how it differs from citizenship
articles.description: Germany offers a permanent settlement permit, distinct from citizenship, granting indefinite residency and work rights. An enhanced European version allows living and working in other EU nations, excluding Denmark and Ireland. While generally requiring B1 German, exceptions exist for integration course graduates or those with specific educational backgrounds. This permit, issued on an electronic card, is typically permanent but can be revoked under certain conditions.

articles.description: Russia claims it has secured two more settlements in eastern Ukraine, marking another reported battlefield advance following Moscow's announcement of the capture of Konstantinovka. According to the Russian Defence Ministry, Russian forces have taken control of Shiykovka in the Kharkiv region and Vasilevka in the Donetsk People's Republic. The ministry released drone footage showing smoke rising over Vasilevka and Russian troops raising the national flag in Shiykovka, claiming Ukrainian positions and reinforcements were destroyed through coordinated drone and artillery strikes.

articles.title: Putin Spokesman Fires At NATO Nation; Zelensky Uses Polish Drones To Attack Russia? 'Horror Stories'
articles.description: Fresh tensions between Russia and NATO are back in the spotlight after Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov responded to reports in British and Polish media claiming Russia could be preparing for an attack on Poland in the coming months. Speaking to Russian journalist Pavel Zarubin, Peskov dismissed the reports as "horror stories" about Russia but accused Poland of hosting companies that manufacture drones later used in attacks against Russian forces. He warned that such activities are taking place on Polish territory and referenced a previous Russian Defence Ministry publication identifying defense-related companies across several European countries.

articles.title: EMOTIONAL: Khamenei’s 3 Sons Break Down In Tears, But No Sign Of Mojtaba At Final Farewell
articles.description: Amid the rigid state protocol, geopolitical threats, and massive political banners of Iran's grand state funeral, one intensely personal moment has captured global attention. The children of the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei were seen breaking down in tears, weeping openly as they bid a final farewell to their father at the Imam Khomeini Grand Mosalla in Tehran. Surrounded by senior military commanders, top clerics, and foreign envoys, the family’s rare public show of raw heartbreak has quickly become some of the most widely shared and emotional footage from the multi-day mourning ceremonies.
